name: Botpress
tagline: An open-source (MIT), developer-first platform for building conversational AI agents with bi-directional MCP support — self-host free, or use the managed cloud from $0/month.
verdict: Botpress is the pick for engineering-led teams that want to own a conversational agent's code and data rather than configure a closed, fully-managed builder: the core framework is genuinely open-source (MIT-licensed, ~14.8k GitHub stars) and free to self-host indefinitely, with bi-directional MCP support and native deployment across a website widget, WhatsApp, Messenger, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Telegram and Twilio voice from one agent definition. The Autonomous Engine (LLMz) lets an agent plan and execute multi-step actions from a single instruction instead of a rigid flow, and a $25M Series B (June 2025, $120M valuation) on top of an earlier Series A signals real staying power for a company this size. The catch is the audience: Botpress is explicit that it isn't a zero-engineering tool — independent reviews describe needing at least one developer to wire up tool calls — and the LLM token cost ("AI Spend") bills separately from the plan fee, often exceeding it in production. Pick Botpress over Botsify if you want an open-source, code-level-customizable platform rather than a smaller no-code builder; pick Dify instead if the priority is a broader RAG/LLMOps workflow rather than conversational-agent channel deployment; pick a fully-managed option like Lindy if the goal is to avoid engineering involvement altogether.
